mechanism: Both drugs are hepatotoxic and can cause hepatic injury through different mechanisms; methimazole causes idiosyncratic hepatotoxicity while pyrazinamide causes dose-dependent hepatotoxicity, increasing cumulative hepatic risk.
action: Monitor liver function tests (AST, ALT, bilirubin) regularly; consider baseline and periodic monitoring during concurrent use; assess risk-benefit ratio and consider alternative anti-tuberculous agents if possible.
